content.text: Both implementations pass through the tainted input unchanged (no sanitization). The value `bar` is derived directly from `param`, which comes from request parameter names, and is concatenated directly into the XPath expression string with no escaping or validation. This is a genuine XPath injection vulnerability — exactly the pattern OWASP Benchmark intends to mark as a true positive for this test ID (vulnerable test cases are typically the odd/designated ones, and this is the classic injectable pattern).

input.justification:
User-controlled data (a request parameter name matching a magic value) flows through ThingFactory/ThingInterface.doSomething (Thing1 and Thing2 implementations both pass the input through unchanged, with no sanitization or encoding) into variable `bar`, which is directly concatenated into an XPath expression string `"/Employees/Employee[@emplid='" + bar + "']"` passed to XPath.evaluate(). There is no validation, escaping, or allow-listing applied to the value before it reaches the XPath sink, so a crafted parameter name could inject XPath syntax, confirming a real XPath injection vulnerability.</justification>
